subject: elephant
reasoning:
I'm sketching out proportions for a stylized elephant model, aiming for about 2.6 m shoulder height, and planning the skeleton hierarchy starting from the hips and spine chain up toward the shoulders.

I'm plotting the spine as a curve from hips to neck base, then sweeping a body mesh along it with elliptical cross-sections, rounded caps at the rump and chest, and a large skull sphere for the head where the trunk will hang down to the ground.

For the legs, I'm setting up straight pillar-like chains with three joints each (hip, knee, foot-top) and naming them so the end becomes a proper tip joint, then sweeping varying radii along each leg and capping with a flattened cylindrical foot.

Now I'm figuring out toenail placement with small boxes near the foot's tip bone, and working out the spine chain parenting so front legs attach near the shoulder joint while hind legs attach near the hips, adjusting the spine joint positions to roughly match the body's z-depth at shoulder and hip.

For the neck and head, I'm planning a short one-span chain from the end of the spine to a neck tip, then adding a separate head joint angled slightly downward, with a rounded sweep connecting body to head. I'm defining the skull as a scaled sphere geometry attached at the head joint.

For the trunk, I'm sketching a curving chain of points dropping from the head down and forward, tapering with a sweep radius that narrows toward the tip, and considering how to add wrinkle rings using alternating color bands along the trunk surface.

Still working out the color palette (greys and lighter tones), the mottled skin paint for the body and legs, and planning a quick flat ear extrusion off the head.

Still refining ear geometry...

Now I'm mapping out the tusk geometry, sweeping curved bezier points from the head outward and forward to a tapered ivory tip, with radius shrinking toward the point and bone-weighted to the head.

Next I'm placing the eyes as small dark spheres on the head sides, computing their position from surface azimuth and elevation on the head ellipsoid rather than fixed coordinates. I also need to add a separate lower jaw part beneath the trunk with its own joint, since the elephant requires a distinct jaw piece.

Now I'm working out the tail: a chain of three bone segments attached at the hips, curving downward and backward from the rump into a hanging path, with a sweep radius that tapers, and a tuft of dark spike cones at the tip for texture.

I'm also planning body shaping details like belly toenails, forehead bumps, and a radius function along the spine chain that tapers between hips, mid-body, and front, with a slight downward shift to suggest belly sag.

Now I'm checking proportions: the neck sweep connects body to head with tapering radii, and I'm verifying that shoulder height, head top, and leg length look anatomically plausible — the legs seem a bit short given the body bottom position relative to the ground.

I'm placing the front and hind legs inside the body ellipse's edge, sizing hip joints and leg chain radii so each limb tapers from thigh to ankle, then capping the tips with a round start and flat end so a foot cylinder can sit flush against the ground.

Adding toenail boxes...

For eyes, I'll place them on the skull surface using azimuth/elevation positioning so they sit on either side symmetrically, with a guard in case the surface lookup fails, then add small dark spheres embedded partway into the socket for the eyeballs.

Now I'm working out the forehead dome placement, a snout bridge sphere where the trunk connects to the head, and the trunk's path geometry—starting it inside the head and extending it forward and down with a curved sweep, parenting the segments to the head and naming them sequentially, with small tip nubs added at the very end.

For the trunk tip, I'm adding tiny finger-like spheres and tapering the sweep radius down toward the end. I'm also setting up a mottled paint pattern for the trunk that alternates between two coat colors based on position, checking that the mottle and paint utilities are properly exported, and defining hinge joints for the ears that aim outward along the x-axis before finishing up floor clearance checks and writing the module.

I'm shaping the skull using a scaled sphere geometry rather than relying on the part's own scale argument, setting up a jaw joint near the chin with a lower jaw part attached, and preparing to apply coat paints to the neck and body sweeps before finalizing and exporting the module.
